import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Set style
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(16, 12))

# Create subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(16, 12))

# 1. Income distribution by education level
income_edu_data = df[df['Income'] < 200000]  # Remove extreme outliers for better visualization
sns.boxplot(data=income_edu_data, x='Education', y='Income', ax=axes[0, 0], palette='viridis')
axes[0, 0].set_title('Income Distribution by Education Level', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Education Level', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Annual Income ($)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 2. Spending categories comparison
spending_cols = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
spending_totals = df[spending_cols].sum()
spending_df = pd.DataFrame({'Category': spending_totals.index, 'Total_Spending': spending_totals.values})
spending_df['Category'] = spending_df['Category'].str.replace('Mnt', '').str.replace('Prods', ' Products')

axes[0, 1].bar(spending_df['Category'], spending_df['Total_Spending'], color=plt.cm.Set3(np.arange(len(spending_df))))
axes[0, 1].set_title('Total Spending by Product Category', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[0, 1].set_xlabel('Product Category', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('Total Spending ($)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 3. Purchase channels comparison
purchase_cols = ['NumWebPurchases', 'NumCatalogPurchases', 'NumStorePurchases']
purchase_means = df[purchase_cols].mean()
purchase_df = pd.DataFrame({'Channel': purchase_means.index, 'Average_Purchases': purchase_means.values})
purchase_df['Channel'] = purchase_df['Channel'].str.replace('Num', '').str.replace('Purchases', '')

colors = ['#FF6B6B', '#4ECDC4', '#45B7D1']
wedges, texts, autotexts = axes[1, 0].pie(purchase_df['Average_Purchases'], labels=purchase_df['Channel'], 
                                          colors=colors, autopct='%1.1f%%', startangle=90)
axes[1, 0].set_title('Average Purchases by Channel', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
for autotext in autotexts:
    autotext.set_color('white')
    autotext.set_fontweight('bold')

# 4. Customer demographics: Marital status distribution
marital_counts = df['Marital_Status'].value_counts()
marital_df = pd.DataFrame({'Status': marital_counts.index, 'Count': marital_counts.values})

sns.barplot(data=marital_df, x='Status', y='Count', ax=axes[1, 1], palette='muted')
axes[1, 1].set_title('Customer Distribution by Marital Status', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Marital Status', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('Number of Customers', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# Add value labels on bars
for i, v in enumerate(marital_df['Count']):
    axes[1, 1].text(i, v + 20, str(v), ha='center', va='bottom', fontweight='bold')

# Adjust layout and save
plt.suptitle('Customer Segmentation Analysis Dashboard', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
